::: {.assignment-intro}
This study combines life-expectancy data from Our World in Data with income-inequality data from the World Bank to examine national patterns between 1990 and 2020. It uses longitudinal summaries and cross-sectional comparisons to ask whether more equal societies tend to experience longer life spans.

## Key findings

- Income inequality and life expectancy have a moderate negative correlation in the assembled country-year data (`r = -0.45`).
- Average life expectancy rose over the study period while the average Gini coefficient declined slightly.
- Countries with Gini coefficients below 0.30 commonly achieved life expectancy above 80 years, whereas countries above 0.45 often recorded life expectancy below 70 years.
- The association is persistent but does not establish causation; geography, development, health systems, and other factors also shape outcomes.
